result:
Before I sanity-check the timeline, one thing stands out that I'd push back on: closing this with the circuit breaker still disabled.

**The concurrency limit and the circuit breaker are not equivalent risks.** Dialing concurrency back down later is a tuning cleanup — fine to note and move on. Leaving the circuit breaker off in front of the ledger service is a different category: that breaker exists specifically to protect a financial system from cascading failure, and right now nothing is watching that boundary. A few concrete concerns:

- **Was it actually just concurrency that cleared the backlog, or did removing the breaker mask a real problem?** If the ledger service was degrading and the breaker would normally have tripped, you may just not be seeing it because the safety net is gone — "dashboards green" could mean "no longer measuring the thing that would tell you."
- **Data integrity during the window.** With the breaker off and concurrency way up, did the ledger service see elevated error rates, timeouts, or retries that could produce duplicate or partial writes? Worth pulling ledger-side logs/metrics for the exact window the breaker was disabled, not just consumer-side backlog metrics.
- **Dana's thumbs-up** — worth confirming what that was actually approving. A reaction to "backlog is back to normal" in a channel is not the same as sign-off on "we're going to leave the ledger circuit breaker disabled." If it was the latter, say so explicitly in the postmortem with a name attached; if it was the former, don't imply it covered the breaker decision.
- **March precedent** — did that incident also involve disabling the ledger circuit breaker, or just bumping concurrency? If March was concurrency-only, this isn't actually "the same playbook," it's a superset with a new risk that wasn't validated last time.

My recommendation: re-enable the circuit breaker (or get explicit, named sign-off to leave it off with a ticket and expiry if there's a real reason), and pull ledger-side error/timeout data for the window it was off, before marking this resolved. That's a blocking item, not a follow-up note — unlike the concurrency limit.

For the timeline itself — I don't have access to your dashboards/incident channel, so send me the actual entries (timestamps, who did what, when backlog recovered, when breaker was flipped off/back) and I'll check it for gaps or inconsistencies and help structure the postmortem doc.
